title: Misc / Often Missed
description: Common service exposure and information disclosure checks.

attacks.name: Missing security.txt
attacks.desc: A missing security.txt file can make the intended vulnerability disclosure channel harder to discover; it is not itself a security breach.
attacks.prevention: Publish a security.txt contact channel to help responsible disclosure, while keeping the actual security policy available elsewhere.

attacks.name: Directory listing
attacks.desc: Automatic directory indexes can reveal files that were not linked from the application.
attacks.prevention: Disable automatic directory listing and ensure private files are outside the public document root.

attacks.name: OPTIONS verb disclosure
attacks.desc: OPTIONS responses can reveal supported methods, which still require proper authorization checks.
attacks.prevention: Allow only required methods and enforce authorization consistently; hiding OPTIONS alone is not a defense.

attacks.name: TRACE / XST
attacks.desc: TRACE reflects request data and is commonly disabled where it serves no operational purpose.
attacks.prevention: Disable TRACE unless operationally required and verify sensitive headers are not reflected to untrusted clients.

attacks.name: WebDAV enabled
attacks.desc: Exposed WebDAV methods may permit file listing or writes if authentication and permissions are weak.
attacks.prevention: Disable WebDAV when unused; otherwise require authentication and restrict write methods and paths.

attacks.name: .well-known/openid-configuration
attacks.desc: OIDC discovery metadata identifies provider endpoints and supported features; public exposure is often intentional.
attacks.prevention: Review OIDC discovery output for sensitive metadata, but keep standards-required public fields available when needed.

attacks.name: /health, /metrics exposure
attacks.desc: Public health or metrics endpoints can reveal infrastructure details when they include sensitive data.
attacks.prevention: Require authentication for detailed health and metrics endpoints and remove sensitive labels or secrets.

attacks.name: /actuator/* (Spring)
attacks.desc: Spring Actuator endpoints can disclose environment, mapping, or diagnostic data if exposed too broadly.
attacks.prevention: Expose only essential Spring Actuator endpoints and protect them with authentication and network controls.

attacks.name: Django /__debug__/
attacks.desc: A public Django debug toolbar can reveal request, SQL, and configuration details.
attacks.prevention: Disable Django debug mode and debug toolbar in production deployments.

attacks.name: Laravel Ignition RCE
attacks.desc: Affected Laravel Ignition installations can expose dangerous debug functionality when deployed insecurely.
attacks.prevention: Update affected Laravel components, disable debug mode, and do not expose Ignition tooling publicly.

attacks.name: Rails /rails/info
attacks.desc: Rails information pages may disclose framework or environment details when accessible in production.
attacks.prevention: Disable public Rails information pages in production and avoid leaking environment details.

attacks.name: Next.js _next/data
attacks.desc: Next.js data endpoints can reveal build identifiers or page data that should still be authorization checked.
attacks.prevention: Authorize every Next.js data endpoint that returns private information, regardless of its build ID or route.

attacks.name: Vite dev server
attacks.desc: An exposed Vite development server can serve source files and development-only tooling.
attacks.prevention: Do not expose Vite's development server to the internet; publish only the production build.

attacks.name: Webpack source maps
attacks.desc: Production source maps can reveal readable source and internal comments from bundled JavaScript.

attacks.name: Swagger/OpenAPI exposure
attacks.desc: Public API documentation can disclose available operations; sensitive methods still need authorization.

attacks.name: GraphQL playground live
attacks.desc: A public GraphQL playground can aid schema exploration and query testing if production access is unrestricted.

attacks.name: phpMyAdmin / Adminer
attacks.desc: Public database administration tools can expose a high-value login surface or data if poorly protected.

attacks.name: Kibana / Grafana open
attacks.desc: Public dashboards can reveal telemetry or administrative controls when authentication is missing.

attacks.name: Exposed .env variants
attacks.desc: Additional .env filename variants can expose secrets if served as static files.

attacks.name: Docker Compose labels
attacks.desc: Container labels may disclose internal service names or deployment metadata.

attacks.name: robots.txt disallow leaks
attacks.desc: Disallow rules in robots.txt can reveal paths even though they do not grant access.

attacks.name: Sitemap with params
attacks.desc: A sitemap may list old endpoints or parameterized URLs that deserve access review.

attacks.name: Wayback old endpoints
attacks.desc: Archived web pages can reveal endpoints that are still reachable but no longer linked.

attacks.name: Google dork
attacks.desc: Search engine operators can reveal indexed files or routes that were unintentionally public.

attacks.name: GitHub dork
attacks.desc: Code search can find committed secrets or configuration paths in public repositories.

attacks.name: Shodan/Censys
attacks.desc: Internet-wide service indexes may list reachable hosts and historical banners.

attacks.name: Favicon hash (Shodan)
attacks.desc: A favicon hash can link a web interface to other hosts indexed with the same icon.

attacks.name: ASN enumeration
attacks.desc: Autonomous system records help identify address ranges associated with an organization.

attacks.name: Reverse DNS sweep
attacks.desc: Reverse DNS records can reveal hostnames for known IP ranges.

attacks.name: SNMP public
attacks.desc: An SNMP service using a public community string may disclose network inventory and configuration.

attacks.name: NFS exports
attacks.desc: Public NFS exports can expose file shares if host restrictions are weak.

attacks.name: rsync open
attacks.desc: An unauthenticated rsync module can reveal or allow changes to synchronized files.

attacks.name: Redis unauth
attacks.desc: An exposed Redis instance without authentication may permit reads or writes to application state.

attacks.name: Memcached unauth
attacks.desc: An exposed Memcached instance may reveal cached data or permit cache manipulation.

attacks.name: MongoDB unauth
attacks.desc: An exposed MongoDB service without authentication may allow database access.

attacks.name: Elasticsearch open
attacks.desc: An exposed Elasticsearch API can reveal indices or documents without authentication.
